Latin word

dominus

dominus, dominī m.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

the boss, the owner; host of a dinner (with or without convīviī, epulī); the owner; a landlord; master, owner

In this lexicon

  • employer

    also used · classical · Traupman 282: boss (owner); Levi–Bini p. 51: principale, the head of a firm

  • host

    also used · classical · Cic. Vatin. 13; Liv. 23.8 (Lewis & Short)

  • landlord

    the recommended word · classical · Suet. Jul. 41.3: vīcātim per dominōs īnsulārum, street by street, through the landlords of the blocks of flats; Cic. Phil. 2.105: tē inquilīnō (nōn enim dominō), with you as tenant (for you were not the owner)

  • master

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Off. 1.139: nec domō dominus, sed dominō domus honestanda est; Cato Agr. 5.3 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 162, 282: boss (owner), dominus

Examples

  • Recēnsum populī nec mōre nec locō solitō, sed vīcātim per dominōs īnsulārum ēgit

    He took the count of the people neither in the usual way nor in the usual place, but street by street, through the landlords of the blocks of flatsSuet. Jul. 41.3

    In the entry for landlord

  • nec domō dominus, sed dominō domus honestanda est

    the master should not be honoured by his house, but the house by its masterCic. Off. 1.139 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for master

  • Quis est dominus hujus canis?

    Who owns this dog?composed

    In the entry for master
